title: Meeting Room Scheduler
summary: Book office meeting rooms without overlaps, search for free rooms by capacity and equipment, auto-book the best fit and show free gaps in a day.
statement:
An office of 200 people keeps double-booking its meeting rooms. Facilities wants a small program that books rooms reliably and helps people find a free room that suits their meeting.

**Rooms**
Each room has a unique name (names are compared ignoring case), a seating capacity and a set of equipment drawn from: projector, whiteboard, video-conferencing.

**Bookings**
- A booking is for one room on one date, from a start time to an end time, made by an organiser for a number of attendees.
- Start and end must fall on 15-minute boundaries (10:00, 10:15, …), lie within office hours 08:00–20:00 on that date, and the end must be after the start.
- The room must seat all attendees (at least 1).
- A booking may not overlap another booking of the same room. Times are half-open: a meeting ending at 11:00 does not clash with one starting at 11:00.
- Only the organiser can cancel a booking; the time becomes free immediately.

**Finding rooms**
- People can search for rooms that are free for a whole time range on a date, seat at least N people and have all the required equipment. Results are ordered by capacity, smallest first, then by name, so small meetings don't take big rooms.
- People can ask for "any suitable room": the program books the first room the search would return, or fails if there is none.
- For a room and a date, people can see its bookings in start-time order and its free gaps within office hours.

Facilities has mentioned that recurring weekly meetings and new kinds of equipment are likely next.

requirements.text: Add rooms with a unique name (case-insensitive), a capacity from 1 to 100 and a set of equipment (projector, whiteboard, video-conferencing). A duplicate name or invalid capacity is rejected.

Book a named room for a date, start, end, organiser and attendee count. Reject times off 15-minute boundaries, outside 08:00–20:00, or with end not after start; attendee counts below 1 or above capacity; and any overlap with an existing booking of that room (half-open intervals). Success returns a booking id.

Search for rooms free for a whole time range on a date that seat at least N people and have all required equipment, ordered by capacity ascending then name. No matches gives an empty list, not an error.

Book any suitable room: with the same inputs as a search plus an organiser, book the first room the search returns and report which room was booked, or fail with a clear reason when the search is empty.
Cancel a booking by id: only its organiser may cancel; unknown or already-cancelled bookings are rejected. The slot is free for new bookings immediately.
List a room's bookings for a date in start-time order, with organiser, times and attendee count.
List a room's free gaps for a date within office hours, in time order, merging adjacent free time into a single gap.

constraints: Java 17 or later using only the standard library; JUnit 5 may be used for tests.
Single JVM process with all state in memory; no database, calendar service, network or frameworks.
One office in one time zone; times are local times of day with 15-minute granularity.
assumptions: Organisers are identified by a non-empty name or id and are trusted; there is no authentication.
Bookings in the past do not need to be rejected, so the program never needs to read the clock.
Rooms are never removed or changed after being added.

examples.title: Overlap and back-to-back
examples.scenario: Rooms: Everest (10 seats; projector, video-conferencing), K2 (4 seats; whiteboard), Nilgiri (6 seats; projector, whiteboard). On 2026-11-02 Alice books K2 10:00–11:00 for 3; Bob books K2 10:30–11:30 for 2; Bob books K2 11:00–12:00 for 2.
examples.expected: Alice's booking succeeds. Bob's first request is rejected because it overlaps 10:00–11:00. Bob's second request succeeds: back-to-back bookings are allowed.

examples.title: Searching
examples.scenario: On the same date: search 10:15–10:45 for 4 people with no equipment; search 12:00–12:30 for 4 people with no equipment; search 12:00–12:30 for 4 people needing a projector.
examples.expected: First search: [Nilgiri, Everest] (K2 is booked). Second: [K2, Nilgiri, Everest]. Third: [Nilgiri, Everest] (K2 has no projector).

examples.title: Any suitable room
examples.scenario: Carol asks for any suitable room on 2026-11-02, 14:00–15:00, for 8 people with video-conferencing. Then Dan asks for any room 14:30–15:30 for 8 people with no equipment.
examples.expected: Carol gets Everest. Dan’s request fails: Everest is the only room seating 8 and it is taken from 14:00 to 15:00.

examples.title: Free gaps and cancellation
examples.scenario: After the first example, list K2's bookings and free gaps on 2026-11-02. Bob tries to cancel Alice's booking; then Alice cancels it and the free gaps are listed again.
examples.expected: Bookings: 10:00–11:00 (Alice), 11:00–12:00 (Bob). Free gaps: 08:00–10:00 and 12:00–20:00. Bob's cancellation is rejected. After Alice cancels, the free gaps are 08:00–11:00 and 12:00–20:00.

edgeCases: A booking 19:30–20:15 or 07:45–08:30 crosses office hours and is rejected; 19:45–20:00 is accepted.
A start time of 10:10 is not on a 15-minute boundary and is rejected.
A start equal to the end, or an end before the start, is rejected.
Zero attendees, or more attendees than the room seats, is rejected.
A booking that exactly fills the gap between two existing bookings is accepted.
Cancelling an unknown or already-cancelled booking, or cancelling as someone other than the organiser, is rejected.
Adding a room named "k2" when "K2" exists is rejected as a duplicate.
outOfScope: Calendar invitations or integration with email/calendar services.
Authentication and permissions beyond the organiser check.
Persistence, REST APIs or any UI.

concurrency.notes: Not assessed. The program may assume requests arrive one at a time from a single thread.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Overlapping bookings of the same room are rejected while back-to-back bookings are accepted, exactly as in the first example.
Time-rule violations (off-boundary, outside office hours, end not after start) and attendee-count violations are each rejected with a clear reason.
Searches return exactly the rooms free for the whole range with enough seats and all required equipment, ordered by capacity then name, as in the second example.
Booking any suitable room books the smallest fitting room and fails with a reason when none fits, as in the third example.
Only the organiser can cancel; after cancelling, the slot can be booked again and appears in the free gaps.
A room's bookings for a date are listed in start-time order and its free gaps cover exactly the unbooked part of 08:00–20:00.

stretchGoals.text: Book a meeting weekly for N weeks, all-or-nothing: if any week clashes, nothing is booked and the clashing dates are reported.
When a requested room is busy, suggest the earliest free slot of the same length in that room on the same date.

rubricGuidance.correctness: FR-2 to FR-4 are central: half-open overlap detection, time validation and the search ordering (capacity, then name). Verify the four worked examples exactly.
rubricGuidance.modeling: Look for clear separation between room definitions, a room's bookings for a date, and the search/auto-book logic. Overlap checking should live in exactly one place and be reused by booking, search and free-gap computation.
rubricGuidance.principles: Bookings should only be created or removed through validated operations, so a room can never hold overlapping bookings, and the time-slot rules should be enforced once. Concurrency is not assessed.
rubricGuidance.extensibility: Plausible changes named in the statement: recurring meetings and new kinds of equipment. Adding an equipment kind should not require changes to search logic. A direct, simple design is perfectly acceptable; speculative abstraction should not earn credit.
rubricGuidance.readability: Time ranges should be represented clearly rather than as ad-hoc integer pairs with repeated comparisons; search filters should read like the statement.
rubricGuidance.edge_cases: Check boundary handling: back-to-back bookings, office-hour limits, 15-minute alignment, zero or excess attendees, cancellation by non-organisers, duplicate room names and empty search results.
rubricGuidance.tests: Expect tests for overlap (including touching intervals), search ordering, auto-book failure, cancellation permissions and free-gap computation.
